_expect.name: South Fork of St. Vrain Canyon

co_south_fork_of_st_vrain_canyon.blurb: This granite canyon lies west of Lyons, within easy reach of Boulder and Longmont. Trad is the main event, about two thirds of the climbing, with a good amount of sport and a modest set of boulder problems. Older lines usually follow cracks on slabs and vertical walls, while newer sport routes take faces and big roofs. Most routes fall between 5.8 and 5.11, with some harder lines above. Rock quality varies: the best stone is solid with edges and flakes, and the worst is crumbly and crystalline. Cliffs face many directions, so climbing is possible all year, though summer and fall are the pick. Scout Rock, Trojan Bunny Buttress, Infirmary Slabs and December Wall are among the biggest crags.

ca_june_lake_area.blurb: June Lake is in the Eastern Sierra, around the June Lake Loop, about 50 miles north of Bishop. At roughly 7,600 feet it runs cooler than the better-known bouldering zones lower down. Bouldering is about half the climbing, mostly on volcanic tuff with some granite nearer to town, and most problems are in the lower and middle grades. The rest is roped: top-rope, sport and a little trad, with a bit of ice. Silver Lake is a quartzite crag of mostly easy to moderate routes, 70 to 200 feet long, that faces east-northeast, so it gets early sun and afternoon shade. The rock there has seen little traffic, so some of it is loose. Rush adds more routes nearby.

co_north_table_mountain_golden_cliffs.blurb: North Table Mountain is a cliff band above the town of Golden, built from old lava flows. It faces south and west, which makes it a favorite for winter and cold-weather days. Trad and sport are close to even, with some top-rope options and a few boulder problems. Routes are short, around 60 feet, and often tightly bolted, with many moderates and a range of harder lines into the 5.12s. Most sit between 5.7 and 5.11. Some of the rock is heavily polished and can feel greasy on warm days, and stone near the tops can be loose. The cliff is split into sections such as Brown Cloud Rocks, the Overhang Area, Winterfest Wall and the East Quarry.

co_staunton_state_park.blurb: Staunton State Park is a pine-forest climbing area in the foothills southwest of Denver. Sport routes dominate, roughly two thirds of the total, with a healthy trad and top-rope presence. Grades start at the easy end, but the sweet spot is 5.10 and 5.11, with a strong group of 5.12s and a few 5.13s above that. Trad lines tend to rely on thin cracks and small features, so sparse protection adds to the challenge. Staunton Rocks is the largest zone by far, followed by the Old Mill Area and Dines Cliff, with The Raven and Never Winter Wall holding smaller sets of sport climbs.

co_lumpy_ridge.blurb: Lumpy Ridge is a line of granite formations just north of Estes Park, at around 8,450 feet, with views toward Longs Peak. Trad overwhelmingly rules, with a handful of aid routes and a modest number of boulder problems. The climbing is stiff and technical: flared cracks with fussy gear, thin seams and faint features, and a few bolted slabs. Most routes fall between 5.9 and 5.11, with few true beginner climbs, though some moderate outings exist. Routes are usually two to five pitches long, and Sundance Buttress is the tallest cliff. The Book, Twin Owls, The Pear and Bookmark are among the biggest formations. Weekends can be crowded.

co_south.blurb: This is the southern end of the Boulder Flatirons, running from Bear Canyon toward Eldorado Canyon, and it holds some of the best climbing in the Flatirons with fewer crowds than other sections. Trad is the main style, with a good amount of sport and bouldering mixed in. Grades spread from easy up to the hard end, with the bulk between 5.8 and 5.12, and the toughest sport routes appear on the Slab, Shanahan Crag and Overhang Rock. Fern Canyon is the largest zone, on the northeast side of Bear Peak. Its routes are mostly short face climbs, many facing south, which makes sunny fall and winter days a good bet. Expect a long approach there. The Maiden, Matron and Seal Rock hold longer outings.
